- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, reduce the peak by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction for next 30d horizon.  
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.25 or more) and forecast diverges from 18-day moving average, align forecast to 18-day MA with ±2% buffer.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is > 10% above forecast, assume sentiment is bullish and adjust next forecast upward by 3–5% if sentiment remains positive.  
- If sentiment is flat (±0.05) and forecast is consistently off, use 18-day history as anchor and adjust forecast to match recent trend, not extrapolation.
